newsitem.title: ROMANIA: APOSTLE ANDREW'S RELICS DRAW BIG CROWDS IN ROMANIA.
newsitem.headline: APOSTLE ANDREW'S RELICS DRAW BIG CROWDS IN ROMANIA.

text.p: The nearly 2,000-year-old relics of Apostle Andrew drew huge crowds and campaigning politicians to Romania's northeast city of Iasi on Sunday.

Romanian Orthodox Church leaders had the relics of Andrew -- who is said to have spread the gospel among ancient Romanians -- flown in from Greece to Iasi on saturday, for a week-long religious ceremonies marking a local saint's day.
According to local church leaders, the Apostle's relics should help to hearten Romanians in their bid "to overcome hardship on the eve of the third millennium".
Romanian state television showed incumbent President Ion Iliescu, a confessed free-thinker, among the crowds packing the Iasi metropolitan cathedral on Sunday.
Iliescu ended a tour of northeast Romania, once his electoral stronghold, on his campaign for the November 3 polls.

The skull of Apostle Andrew, encased in a silver casket, was displayed before thousands of worshippers gathered outside the Iasi cathedral, along with the relics of the city's patron saint Paraschiva, who was cannonised in the early Middle Ages.

Hundreds of faithful spent Saturday night outside the cathedral, hoping to catch a first glimpse of the Apostle relics, which Greek Orthodox Church hierarchs flew to Iasi in a goodwill gesture from the northwest Greek port of Patras.

Six of Iliescu's challengers, including his two main rivals, opposition Democratic Convention bloc leader Emil Constantinescu and ex-Prime Minister Petre Roman, are expected to visit Andrew's relics on Monday.
Andrew, one of the 12 Apostles which Christ sent to preach the gospel, is believed to have travelled northward, across what is now Romania's Black Sea coast, around the year 70 A.D.
Official census data show that more than 86 percent of Romanians belong to the mainstream Orthodox church, which has a centuries-old tradition of cooperation with state authorities.
Many Orthodox Romanians worship the relics of local saints, like those of St.Paraschiva, which they believe bring good luck, health or rain to the crops.
